title: AB1910 (2019-2020): Firearms: prohibited persons.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check, California); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text (Introduced 2020-01-08, via LegiScan getBillText)
provenance.note: As introduced 2020-01-08 (no floor vote; this was the only/last saved version). Section 1001.36 also gets non-gun wording changes (consent, danger finding, 'shall not be placed' wording) which are not quoted. Section 2 amends 8103 'as added by Section 2 of Chapter 861 of the Statutes of 2018' (version operative January 1, 2020), and the bill strikes the 'operative on January 1, 2020' sentence (old subdivision (l)) in that version.

operative_text:
Section 1001.36 (Penal Code): (j) Unless granted an exemption pursuant to Section 29855, a defendant who, on or after January 1, 2021, is granted pretrial diversion pursuant to this section for an offense described in Section 29800 or 29805 shall be advised that, pursuant to subdivision (i) of Section 8103 of the Welfare and Institutions Code, the defendant is prohibited from purchasing, receiving, attempting to purchase or receive, or having possession, custody, or control of any firearm. If a defendant was legally incompetent at the time the diversion was granted, the advisement required by this section shall take place upon the defendant’s restoration to competence.
Section 8103 (Welfare and Institutions Code): (i) (1) Unless granted an exemption pursuant to Section 29855 of the Penal Code, a defendant who, on or after January 1, 2021, is granted pretrial diversion pursuant to Section 1001.36 of the Penal Code, for an offense listed in Section 29800 or 29805 of the Penal Code, and is advised by the court as required by subdivision (j) of Section 1001.36 of the Penal Code, shall not purchase or receive, or attempt to purchase or receive, or have possession, custody, or control of any firearm.
Section 8103 (Welfare and Institutions Code): (2) Upon successful completion of diversion, or upon adjudication of reinstated charges, a person may request a hearing from the superior court of their county of residence for an order allowing them to own, possess, control, receive, or purchase a firearm.
Section 8103 (Welfare and Institutions Code): (j) Every person who owns or possesses or has custody or control of, or purchases or receives, or attempts to purchase or receive, any firearm or any other deadly weapon in violation of this section shall be punished by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code or in a county jail for not more than one year.
